scope: the left big toe, toe 2 and the 1–2 web (left is the man's own; every view shows his left foot)

merged.text: In profile the hallux is a thin wedge ending in a point at the nail's free edge, about 14–15 mm thick at the nail root. A real big toe ends in a blunt, domed pulp that bulges forward and down under the nail; this one reads like a beak.
also: In profile the hallux thins to a pointed wedge: the nail's free edge is the foremost point with no pulp ahead of or below it, and the toe is about 14–15 mm thick at the nail root (spec 19) and 20–21 mm at the IP (Jeff's direction about 25).

In medial profile the distal hallux is a thin wedge tapering to a point at the nail (~15.6 mm deep at the nail root against 19). A real hallux ends blunt, with a full rounded pulp bulging below and just beyond the free edge.

The distal hallux is too thin and tapers to a pointed wedge. At 17.9 px/mm the silhouette is ~280 px (~15.6 mm) deep at the nail root against 19 mm, outside +/-2, and ~21 mm at the IP against 22 (~25 after the broadening).

In profile the hallux tapers to a chisel: the dorsal line runs straight to the nail's tip and the pulp is undercut beneath it, where a real big toe ends in a blunt, round pulp below and ahead of the free edge.
Hallux in profile: the dorsal line slopes straight down to the nail's tip and the pulp is undercut beneath it, so the end reads as a chisel or beak instead of a blunt, rounded pulp.
fixes: Thicken the distal phalanx so the dorsum over the nail runs nearly level and the pulp forms a blunt dome reaching as far forward as the free edge and rounding down to the floor, as in the anchor photos.
Keep about 19-20 mm of depth to the nail root, and give the distal phalanx a full rounded pulp that bulges below and just beyond the free edge so the tip ends blunt, not pointed.
The pulp carries forward and down under the free edge as a rounded bulb; in profile the tip is blunt, its front a convex curve below and ahead of the nail.

merged.text: [D5] Both distal corners of the hallux nail are torn, a dark spiky cluster medially and a white saw-tooth zigzag laterally, spiky in clay too and already visible as dark specks at the nail corners in the front and top34 views.
also: Torn geometry at the hallux nail's medial distal corner: a dark cluster of jagged spikes where the plate's corner meets the fold, spiky in clay too and visible as dark specks at native size in the front and top34 views.

Both distal corners of the hallux nail end in jagged grey sawtooth shreds, plain to see in the closeup at native size. Nothing in a real nail corner looks torn: the folds run smooth into the free edge.

Both distal corners of the hallux nail end in jagged grey sawtooth shreds of torn geometry: the medial one boxed here, the lateral at about [1708, 983, 2000, 1314]. Both also show at native size in pair_hr.hallux_eval and at the tip in medial_eval.

Hallux nail, medial distal corner: dark, jagged teeth where the free edge, the medial fold and the hyponychium intersect; the clay shows the same torn geometry (pair_hr.hallux_form.png [952,1387,1097,1449]) and the medial view shows it at the tip.
fixes: The medial nail fold should taper smoothly into the hyponychium under the free-edge corner, the plate passing cleanly beside or under the fold skin, never through it.
Run the lateral folds and the hyponychium smoothly into the free edge's corners with no spiky displacement. A real corner shows only a soft groove and at most a faint dark grime line under the edge.
The free edge overhangs the hyponychium with a clean dark gap, and the medial fold ends in a smooth, rounded corner beside it.

merged.text: The 1–2 web is torn deep on the hallux's lateral wall: a black, ragged slit in the toe 2 closeup and crumpled spikes in clay, where a real web is a smooth U-fold with a soft shadow.
also: Deep in the 1–2 web, on the hallux's lateral wall, the surface is crumpled and torn: jagged spikes in clay and a black ragged slit in the eval render; crinkles also show in the front and top34 clay views.
A strip of torn, spiky geometry in the 1-2 web cleft renders as a black jagged crack beside the hallux. The web is one continuous, smooth fold of skin.

A strip of torn, spiky geometry runs down the 1-2 web cleft where the hallux's lateral side meets the web. In pair_hr.toe2_eval it renders as a black jagged crack (about [197, 98, 248, 362]); it also shows in front_form and top34_form.
Deep in the 1–2 web the hallux's lateral wall is torn: a column of broken, speckled triangles over terraced ripples in the clay, a black jagged slit in the lit toe 2 view.

1–2 web, the hallux's lateral wall deep in the cleft: a column of torn, speckled triangles with terraced ripples below it; in the lit view it is a black jagged slit (pair_hr.toe2_eval.png [197,93,254,352]): surfaces crossing or collapsed in the cleft.
fixes: A real 1–2 web is a smooth U-shaped skin fold with a soft shadow gradient into the cleft, with no self-intersection.
The web is one continuous fold of skin from the hallux's lateral side to toe 2's medial side. Remove the self-intersection or tear so the cleft shades as a smooth, soft crease.
The web is one continuous skin saddle: the hallux's lateral wall curves smoothly down into the web floor and up toe 2's side, with soft creases and nothing folded or overlapping.

merged.text: Both distal corners of the hallux nail tear into sawtooth fringes where plate, folds and hyponychium intersect, white teeth up the lateral fold and dark teeth at the medial corner [D2]; visible at native size in every view of the nail and unmistakably CG.

merged.text: The same tear at the hallux nail's lateral distal corner: a white saw-tooth zigzag, regular as a zip, runs along the fold edge beside the free edge; spiky in clay too.
fixes: A smooth lateral sulcus ending cleanly under the free-edge corner, with no intersection between the plate and the fold.

merged.text: The nails read as press-on tiles: the hallux plate's proximal end is a thick, glossy white lip lying on the skin, with no eponychium or cuticle over it and no crescent lunula. A real proximal fold overlaps the root and the lunula shows as a matte half-moon.
also: No lunula on the hallux: the proximal end of the plate is a straight, full-width, glossy white band with a hard edge, reading as the rim of a stuck-on plate rather than a milky crescent under the cuticle.
No crescent lunula on the hallux: the plate's proximal end is a straight, full-width, glossy white band with a hard lower edge, reading as the exposed rim of a stuck-on plate.

The hallux plate's proximal end is a thick, glossy white lip lying on the skin: no eponychium or cuticle overlaps it, and the pale band is a straight bevelled strip rather than a crescent lunula. It reads as a glued-on press-on nail.

Its root shows a thick white bevel, the plate's own edge thickness, with no cuticle or eponychium lapping over it: a stuck-on acrylic nail. A real plate slides out from under the proximal fold and its root is never seen.

Hallux plate, proximal and medial edges: a thick, bright-white bevel shows the plate's edge thickness at the root, so it reads as a stuck-on acrylic tile; no eponychium or cuticle laps over it and the plate does not vanish under the proximal fold.
fixes: A soft, milky crescent, convex distally and about 3.5 mm deep at the centre, fading toward the lateral folds and partly hidden under a skin-coloured cuticle.
Tuck the root under a proximal fold 1.5 mm wide with a 0.4 mm eponychium and a thin cuticle on the plate, with a matte 3.5 mm half-moon lunula, convex distally, emerging from under it.
A real plate slides out from under the proximal fold, so its root and edge thickness are never seen; a thin, slightly translucent cuticle band lies on the plate's base.

merged.text: From below, the hallux and toe 2 pads are rectangular blocks with straight sides and squared ends; real pulps are oval, fleshy domes, widest mid-pad and rounding into the tip.
also: From below, the hallux pad is a rectangular block with straight parallel sides and a squared-off end, and toe 2's pad is the same in miniature; neither pulp bulges or rounds into its tip.
From below the pulps are blocks: toe 2 is a rectangle with parallel sides and a squared end, the hallux a rounded brick. Real pulps are oval, bulbous pads that narrow to a rounded tip.
From below both pulps are boxy. Toe 2's is a rectangle with parallel sides and a squared, nearly square-cornered end; the hallux pad is a rounded brick with straight sides.
From below, the hallux and toe 2 pads are rounded rectangles with straight sides, square tips and flat faces, no pulp bulge and no neck at the crease; they read as silicone blocks, not pulps.

From below, the hallux and toe 2 pads are rounded rectangles: straight parallel sides, square tips and flat faces, with no pulp bulge and no narrowing toward the flexion crease; tofu blocks, not pulps.
fixes: Real toe pulps are oval, fleshy domes, widest mid-pad and rounding into the tip; the hallux pad is broad and bulbous, pinched into a waist at the IP crease.
Make the pulps oval, bulbous pads, widest over the distal phalanx tuft and narrowing to a rounded arc at the tip, with the soft tissue bulging slightly beyond the bone at the sides.
Real pulps are oval to teardrop cushions, fullest at the pulp centre, narrowing to a neck at the flexion crease, with round tips.

merged.text: Toe 2's nail is combed with bold white longitudinal streaks across the whole plate, like brushed metal; real ridging shows only as a faint ripple in the highlight.
also: Toe 2's nail plate is combed with bold, high-contrast white longitudinal streaks over its whole width, like brushed aluminium or glass fibre.
The nail plates are combed with strong white longitudinal streaks like brushed acrylic. A 40-year-old's ridging is faint and shows only in a raking highlight.

Toe 2's plate is combed with strong white, high-contrast longitudinal streaks like brushed acrylic, and the hallux plate shows the same in its highlight. At 0.01 mm deep these ridges should barely read.

Toe 2's plate is streaked edge to edge with dense, ruler-straight, high-contrast white lines, brushed aluminium rather than keratin, and the skin's cell net shows through it as if the bed were dorsal skin.

Toe 2 plate: covered edge to edge with dense, ruler-straight, high-contrast white streaks, a brushed-aluminium look, and the skin's polygon cell pattern shows through the plate as if the bed were dorsal skin.
fixes: Real longitudinal ridging is about 0.01 mm deep and shows only as a faint ripple in the highlight; the plate reads smooth, pink over the bed and slightly milky.
Keep the ridging at 0.25 mm pitch and about 0.01 mm deep, so it shows only as a faint ripple in a raking highlight, never as white stripes.
Longitudinal ridges are faint and slightly wavy, seen mainly inside the highlight; the bed under the plate is smooth pink with fine lengthwise grooves, never the skin's cell network.

merged.text: Beneath toe 2's free edge the distal groove is a box-cut rectangular slot with vertical walls and a flat floor. The real hyponychium is a shallow, rounded groove.

Toe 2's lateral nail folds stop in square-cut walls at the free-edge corners, leaving dark rectangular slots, and the free edge has a small V-kink at its centre.
Under toe 2's free edge the distal groove is a flat-floored rectangular slot with vertical walls at both ends, as if box-cut into the tip, and the free edge has a small V drip at its centre.
Toe 2's nail drops its medial distal corner into a dark, sharp-walled slot in the skin, where the nail groove should be a soft sulcus opening out at the free edge.
Toe 2 nail, medial distal corner: the plate's corner drops into a dark, sharp-walled rectangular slot cut into the skin, visible at native size (pair_hr.toe2_eval.png [864,1465,911,1594]).
fixes: The lateral folds taper smoothly toward the tip and the free edge rides just beyond the hyponychium, with no pocket around it.
Shape the hyponychium as a shallow, rounded groove where the tip skin meets the underside of the plate, with about 1.2 mm of free edge overhanging it and no straight walls or square corners.
The lateral nail groove is a shallow, soft sulcus that opens out at the free edge, the fold's skin rounding over the plate's corner.

merged.text: Toe 2 is an even tube from knuckle to pulp, with no PIP swelling, no waist over the middle phalanx and four evenly spaced stamped rings: a sausage toe with grooves rather than a jointed one.
also: Toe 2 is an even tube from the PIP to the pulp: straight parallel sides, no knuckle swelling, no waist over the middle phalanx, and four evenly spaced stamped grooves over the PIP.
Toe 2 is a smooth, even cylinder with no PIP knuckle or waist over the middle phalanx. It reads as a finger or sausage rather than a curled second toe with a bony knuckle.

Toe 2 is a smooth cylinder of nearly even width from the PIP to the tip, with no dorsal knuckle at the head of the proximal phalanx and no waist over the middle phalanx. A sausage toe (spec 8.4) that reads as a finger.
fixes: A real second toe swells at the PIP knuckle, narrows over the middle phalanx and widens again at the pulp; its dorsal wrinkles are a loose, irregular cluster of fine lines.
Raise a PIP knuckle (the condyles of the phalanx head under slightly thicker skin), narrow the middle phalanx and let the distal pulp bulge, so the curled toe reads jointed.

merged.text: The hallux IP and toe 2 PIP wrinkles are one stamp: 3–4 identical, evenly spaced, perfectly parallel grooves of equal depth, like bellows; real knuckle skin bunches into irregular, branching, broken creases of mixed depth.
also: Knuckle wrinkles are 3-4 identical, evenly spaced, smoothly carved rings, the same on the hallux IP and toe 2 PIP, and toe 2's DIP is one clean cut. Real creases are irregular, uneven in depth and length, fork, and fade out at the sides.

The hallux IP wrinkles are three identical, evenly spaced, smoothly carved ring grooves. Toe 2's PIP has the same set (about [1056, 279, 1501, 528]) and its DIP a single clean cut: machined and copy-pasted.

Hallux IP wrinkles (and toe 2's PIP set, [1196,637,1423,771]) are one stamp: 3–4 identical, evenly spaced, perfectly parallel grooves of equal depth, crisp in the clay too, like bellows rather than skin.
fixes: Use 3-6 irregular creases per joint, varying in length, depth (~0.2 mm) and spacing, some forking or merging and fading out at the sides, with each joint's set different from the others.
Knuckle skin bunches into irregular, branching, broken creases of mixed length and depth around an oval knuckle pad, with finer criss-cross lines between them.

merged.text: Under toe 2 the PIP flexion crease is a straight, sharp-edged ledge across the whole toe, the distal part stepping up like a sleeve cuff, where real skin forms a soft fold.
also: A straight, hard-edged step runs across toe 2's plantar surface, a seam with a shading break and white specks, unlike any flexion crease.
A straight, hard-edged step runs across toe 2's plantar surface below its proximal crease: a seam with a shading break and white specks at its lateral end, unlike any flexion crease.
Toe 2's plantar PIP crease is a straight, sharp-edged ledge across the full width of the toe: the distal segment steps up like the cuff of a sleeve instead of the skin folding.

A flexed PIP folds the plantar skin into a soft, slightly curved crease (~0.5 mm deep) with rounded lips and a little bunching, fading toward the sides.

merged.text: A long, thin, glossy groove across the first MTP's dorsum reads as a healed cut or scar; real skin there is smooth or carries a few short, soft wrinkles that fade at the sides.
also: A single long, thin, glossy groove crosses the dorsum over the first MTP and reads as a healed cut or scar, not a skin fold.
A single long, sharp-lipped groove crosses the dorsum of the hallux's base like a healed incision; dorsal MTP creases are several soft, shallow, wavy lines.
Dorsum of the hallux's base (1st MTP): a single long, sharp-lipped groove crosses it like a healed incision, not a flexion crease.
fixes: At rest the skin over the first MTP is smooth or carries a few short, soft transverse wrinkles that fade out at the sides.
Dorsal MTP creases are several soft, shallow, wavy lines, deepest when the toe extends, never one sharp groove.

merged.text: The hallux nail, the focus of most views, is a flat tile in a template rounded-rectangle outline sunk in an even groove like an inset panel; with almost no transverse curve it reflects as one blown-out white slab from the side.
also: Hallux plate in clay: a flat tile with a template rounded-rectangle outline set in an even groove like an inset panel; almost no transverse curvature (the matcap is uniform across it), so in the medial view it reflects as one blown-out white slab.

merged.text: Both plates are flat rounded squares set in rectangular pockets. A hallux nail with an 11 mm transverse radius (6 mm on toe 2) is clearly domed side to side, its lateral edges diving into the nail grooves under soft folds.
also: The hallux plate is a flat rounded square in a rectangular pocket, its matcap shading uniform edge to edge, and toe 2's plate is the same. Neither has the transverse dome of its 11 mm or 6 mm radius.
fixes: Dome each plate side to side to its radius (about 6 mm of sag across the 19.5 mm hallux nail) and let its lateral edges sink under soft lateral folds into the nail grooves rather than standing on a ledge.

merged.text: The hallux nail is a press-on: a flat rounded-square tile with a straight proximal edge, tight corners and a bright, even French tip. A real big-toe nail is convex, meets a curved cuticle line and ends in an ivory, slightly uneven free edge.
also: The hallux nail reads as a press-on: a flat, evenly lit rounded-square tile with a straight proximal edge, tight proximal corners and a bright, even white French-tip band.
fixes: A real big-toe plate is clearly convex (about 11 mm radius) and darkens toward its sides, meets a curved cuticle line with no proximal corners, and ends in an ivory free edge of slightly uneven width with a faint grey line beneath.

merged.text: The hallux free edge is an even, opaque, milk-white band with a rolled, wavy bead: a French-manicure tip. A trimmed toenail edge is cut, slightly irregular, translucent off-white keratin with a faint grime line under it.
also: Hallux free edge: an even, opaque, milk-white band with a rolled, wavy bead (clay zoom), like a French-manicure tip; no cut keratin face, no translucency at the margin, no yellowing and no grime line beneath.
fixes: A trimmed toenail edge is cut, slightly irregular off-white to yellowish keratin, translucent at the margin and square-faced in section, with a faint dark line under it.

merged.text: The plantar friction ridges are straight parallel stripes at one angle over the sole and both pads, running straight over the flexion creases like corduroy. Real pads carry a whorl, loop or arch each, with forks and endings, and the ridges stop at the creases.

merged.text: From below the hallux grows straight out of the ball with no base crease. A real sole shows a deep curved fold where the toe's pad meets the ball under the first metatarsal head.

merged.text: No hair: no tuft on the hallux's proximal phalanx and none on toe 2. The hairier anchor feet carry dark hairs there; bald toes read young and mannequin-like.
also: No hair: the hallux's proximal phalanx has no tuft and toe 2 none of its few hairs, so the toes read hairless and young beside the anchor photos.
fixes: 8–12 dark hairs 5–8 mm long lying flat toward the tip on the hallux's proximal phalanx, and 2–4 short hairs on toe 2's.

merged.text: The hallux plate is one milky grey-pink from root to edge: no lunula, no pink bed under a clear plate, no paler band before the free edge, so it reads as frosted plastic laid on the toe.
also: Hallux plate colour: one uniform milky grey-pink from root to free edge; no lunula, no pink bed reading through a clear plate, no paler band before the free edge, so it reads as frosted plastic laid on the toe.

merged.text: The 1–2 web's margin is a long, straight, hard edge, a flat shelf jutting between the toes like a cut plane; a real web is a soft U-shaped saddle set back in the cleft, curling under to the plantar side.
also: 1–2 web margin: a long, straight, hard edge, a flat shelf jutting between the toes like a cut plane, with no saddle curve, no fold and no creases where the skin turns under to the plantar side.

merged.text: The toe skin is a uniform crackle of dark-outlined polygons about twice the spec's size (0.4-0.9 against 0.25-0.4 mm), equally deep everywhere and continuing over the tip: crazed porcelain or lizard skin rather than human skin lines.
also: The toe skin is a uniform crackle of dark-outlined polygons about 40-90 px (0.4-0.9 mm at 98 px/mm) against the spec's 0.25-0.4 mm, equally deep everywhere and continuing over the tip: crazed porcelain or lizard skin.

merged.text: A crisp ring-like step crosses toe 2's plantar middle phalanx between its creases, smooth above and ridged below, so the tip reads as a thimble glued on where two meshes or methods meet.

fixes: Skin runs continuously along the toe: no step and no change of texture between the creases; only the true flexion creases mark the plantar side.

merged.text: The hallux IP wrinkles are three identical, evenly spaced parallel grooves, like one sculpted stroke repeated; real knuckle skin has a loose cluster of fine, broken, unequal lines.
also: The hallux IP wrinkles are three identical, evenly spaced, parallel smooth grooves, like one sculpted stroke repeated.

merged.text: Under the hallux's base the plantar outline is pinched into a sharp V-notch with a hard lip, as if the toe were a tube joined to the foot; the digito-plantar crease is a soft fold under a bulging pad.

merged.text: A thin, raised, glossy line arcs across the first MTP dorsum. A podiatrist would read it as a healed bunionectomy incision rather than a skin crease.
also: A single thin, raised, glossy line arcs across the dorsum of the first MTP joint and reads as a healed bunionectomy incision scar. It also shows in top34_eval at about [414, 507, 693, 652].

merged.text: The tendons stop short: the EHL ridge fades before the first MTP, no extensor slip shows toward toe 2, and the forefoot dorsum in frame has no veins at all, where a lean soldier's foot shows dorsal metatarsal veins.

A small round bead like a blister sits on the hallux's proximal nail fold, best seen in the clay views (front_form, top34_form, hallux_form).

A small round bead sits on the hallux's proximal nail fold at the plate's medial corner, a lump that follows no anatomy (also pair_hr.top34_form.png [1097,1201,1144,1237] and pair_hr.front_form.png).
fixes: The eponychium is an even, thin roll of skin along the whole cuticle line.
The eponychium is an even, continuous rim along the plate's root, with no bulges.

merged.text: Pinch marks dimple both pulps' tips in the clay, like mesh poles: a short crease on the hallux pulp and an X-shaped pinch on toe 2's.

merged.text: The declared first-pass skin distorts the pads: the plantar ridges are one field of straight, parallel diagonal stripes at a single angle across both pulps and the sole, like corduroy, with no whorls or loops; in the medial view they band the toe like contour lines.

merged.text: Also the declared material: the dorsal crackle is coarse, dark-lined crazing like cracked glaze, even over the toes, nail folds, hyponychium and pulp tips, and it shows through toe 2's plate on the nail bed.

The toes read young and clean, close to a mannequin's: the hallux is puffy and evenly rounded with no bony IP condyles, and both proximal phalanges are hairless (hair itself is outside this round's questions).

The toes read young and clean: one even pink-beige, a wet, oily sheen on the dorsum, no redness over the knuckles, no dryness at the tips or nail folds. Mostly the declared material, but it makes the scope a foot model's, not a 40-year-old soldier's.

The declared first-pass skin also hides the toes' surface: an even crackle-glaze net of equal polygon cells covers everything, crisp on toe 2 and the web and faint on the hallux, under a wet sheen and with no pores; real toe skin has fine oriented furrows and smoother tips.
No veins at the toe bases or on the forefoot: the anchors' lean male feet show a dorsal venous network running toward the webs; here only the extensor ridges give the dorsum any relief.

The free edges are perfectly smooth, glossy, opaque white bands with rounded bevels, like a French manicure. A trimmed toenail's edge is ivory, matte, a little irregular, with a faint grime line beneath.

The toes read younger and cleaner than a boot-wearing 40-year-old's: pristine template nails with no thickening, trim marks or wear, perfectly even folds, and no hair tuft on the hallux or toe 2 (hair is outside this round): a mannequin or prosthetic read.
